channel.title: The Imaginative Conservative - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Imaginative Conservative (theimaginativeconservative.org)

item.title: Roman Concord: St. Clement of Rome’s Famous Letter
item.description: The Letter of Clement provides our first glimpse of the Gospel fused with 'Romanitas'—a vision of Rome not so much as a symbol of strength and power as of unity and peace. Whereas the old 'Pax Romana' was achieved through conquest and force, the new order would be built on the love of Jesus. (essay by Michael De Sapio)

item.title: "Adelaide"
item.description: Beethoven wrote "Adelaide," a song for solo voice and piano, when he was in his mid-twenties. The theme of the poem that provides the text for the song—the yearning for an unattainable woman—would indeed become the animating theme of Beethoven's love life. (song by Ludwig van Beethoven)

item.title: Paul Kingsnorth's "Against the Machine"
item.description: Paul Kingsnorth believes that the Machine Age has replaced the four P's of traditional culture (the past, the people, place, and prayer) with four S's: science, self, sex, and the screen. (essay by Chuck Chalberg)

item.title: Four Hours of Fury: The Story of World War II's Operation Varsity
item.description: The Rhine River was the line of no return—once the paratroopers of the 17th Airborne crossed it, they’d be over enemy territory. Some pretended to sleep while others smoked or just stared into space. No one spoke. The roar of the engines and the rattling of the airframe made conversation impossible, which was just fine. Most were dwelling on their own thoughts anyway. (book excerpt by James M. Fenelon)

item.title: How to Pray in Mystical Contemplation
item.description: The offering of ourselves that we make is a “true” and therefore acceptable offering when it is made with a “pure and humble heart”. When we learn to thank, praise, adore and glorify him for who he is and for what his love has done for us, then we are learning the meaning of true selfless loving. (essay by David Torkington)

item.title: Good Tree
item.description: At the beginning of Holy Week, we see Jesus, the New Adam, as he prepares for his Passion, beneath a fig tree. Yet it was not the fruit that cursed the man—there was none—but the God-man who cursed the tree. How should we understand this? (essay by Br. Clement Greenspan)

item.title: "Lo, the Full, Final Sacrifice": Music for Holy Week
item.description: My own continued admiration of Gerald Finzi’s majestic and moving anthem, "Lo, The Full, Final Sacrifice," lies not only in the masterful blend of music and words, but also in the confluence of so many personal memories that touch and move me. (essay by Dwight Longenecker)

item.title: Satan’s Empty Show
item.description: With eyes that pierce every illusion, Jesus saw us drowning in this stupor of gnawing desires and lies. To snatch our attention out of the swamp, he suffered a death of such torture and abandonment that it shocks us. (essay by Gabriel O'Neill)

item.title: The Abolition of the Hereditary Lords & the Death of England
item.description: The determined move to abolish the hereditary lords is part of a process of self-destruction. The lords are part of the mythical bulwark that sustains England. (essay by John Horvat)

item.title: I Shall Surely Betray Thee
item.description: While we are in this sojourning to our true homeland, we are not fixed immovably in the love of God. Only in heaven, with the blessed, will we see God and his goodness in all of its contours; and once seen, we will desire nothing else. (essay by Sebastian Vicente)

item.title: The Last Supper and the Origins of Christian Belief
item.description: Our faith tells us, and we believe, that the Presence of the Lord is not just a thing of the past. He is with us now, in the present. (essay by Robert Batule)

item.title: John With Jesus: From Passover to the Garden of Gethsemane
item.description: Jesus prayed so intensely that he sweated, then his sweat turned to blood. As he prayed even longer, his body began to sway. He was shaking. From the thin blue night air, two angels suddenly materialized next to him. (story by Barbara J. Elliott)

item.title: The Triduum That Changed My Life
Good Words on a Good Friday
item.description: The “Seven Last Words of Christ" can seen as the verbal expression of an interior reality: namely, the mind of Christ, as formed according to a deeply ingrained, habitual life practice of living mindfully according to the Lord’s Prayer... (essay by Christopher Morrissey)

item.title: The Brilliant Darkness of a Friday Afternoon
item.description: Not only did Jesus manifest Himself as the Logos so long desired in the pagan West on that Friday afternoon, but He also manifested Himself as the Christ, the true and eternal king. In some mysterious way, it was the death on Friday that revealed all of this, not the resurrection on Sunday. (essay by Bradley Birzer)
